lines:
Responsibilities: Owns trusted-extension installed-version records and contribution identity, verifies manifest/integrity/compatibility facts, distinguishes missing from incompatible or disabled requirements, and attests host process generations before use.
Owned state: ExtensionRecordV1 with stable extensionId, version, manifest schema, Aworkit compatibility range, entry point, contribution descriptors, configuration schema, dependency/provenance facts, content hash/signature status where available, enabled state, and last attested host generation.
Public commands/events and ports: DiscoverManifestsInert, RegisterInstalledExtension, EnableExtension, DisableExtension, RemoveRecord, ResolveContribution, VerifyIntegrity, CheckCompatibility, PinForSnapshot, and AttestHostHandshake; emits ExtensionInventoryChangedV1 and CompatibilityChangedV1 without executing code.
Invariants: discovery and workflow import are inert; installation and enabling are separate explicit decisions. Enabled third-party code is trusted with desktop-user OS authority and may bypass mediated brokers; subprocess isolation is not described as security isolation. Each Run pins exact identity/version/hash, and an update is new trusted code. Unknown workflow nodes remain losslessly preserved and inactive.
Transactional and failure behavior: inventory updates use expected versions and atomic manifest/hash records. Hash/identity mismatch, incompatible protocol, disappeared entry point, or failed handshake quarantines the contribution and blocks new dispatch without mutating existing workflow JSON. A running pinned version is never silently substituted.
NFRs: deterministic compatibility resolution, fast indexed lookup, bounded discovery without execution, hash/provenance audit trail, cross-platform path handling, and clear diagnostics.
Non-responsibilities: no plugin marketplace/automatic install, code execution, sandbox enforcement, capability authorization, secret distribution, or workflow rewriting.

data.name: Extension Identity, Integrity & Compatibility Registry
data.technology: Rust manifest registry, hash verifier, compatibility resolver, and process attestation
